title: Choreographic Works
summary: Individual choreographic works are name-title or title headings from the name authority file. Headings covering several related choreographic works sharing music/story (or where the individual work cannot be determined) are LCSH topical headings (150) entered under the common English title (else original-language title) and qualified "(Choreographic work)", with BT Dance. Such multi-work headings were in the name authority file until 2015.
validation_rules: Headings for several related choreographic works (or where the individual work cannot be determined) are topical headings of the form `[title] (Choreographic work)`, e.g. `Rite of spring (Choreographic work)`, `Romeo and Juliet (Choreographic work)`. (H 1366.5 sec. 1.a, 1.c)
The title in such a heading is the one commonly found in English-language reference sources; if none is found, the original-language title. (H 1366.5 sec. 1.a)
The qualifier is exactly `(Choreographic work)` (singular). (H 1366.5 sec. 1.a)
Broader term for these headings is `Dance`. (H 1366.5 sec. 1.b)

Resources about an individual choreographic work get the name-title or title heading from the name authority file, e.g. `Balanchine, George. Mozartiana`, `Petipa, Marius, 1818-1910. Giselle--Illustrations`. (H 1366.5 sec. 2.a)
Multi-work choreographic headings were established in the name authority file until 2015; those are to be replaced by the LCSH `(Choreographic work)` headings. (H 1366.5 Background)

sections.heading: 1. Establishing headings that cover several related choreographic works
a. Form of heading
sections.text: Establish a topical heading (MARC tag 150) representing several choreographic works under the title by which the works are commonly found in English-language reference sources. If the title is not found in English-language reference sources, establish the heading in the original language of the work. Qualify the heading by *(Choreographic work)*.

sections.heading: b. References
sections.text:
(1) UF references. Add 4XX fields following the general guidelines in H 373.

(2) Broader terms. Provide the 550 (broader term) reference *Dance*.

sections.heading: c. Examples
sections.text:
```
150 ## $a Rite of spring (Choreographic work)
550 ## $w g $a Dance
[Stravinsky composed the music, which has been choreographed by Nijinsky, Collins,
Vesak, and others]

150 ## $a Romeo and Juliet (Choreographic work)
550 ## $w g $a Dance
[Prokofiev composed the music, which has been choreographed by Balanchine,
Burgoine, and others; other musical pieces based on Shakespeare's play have also
been composed, such as Constant Lambert's piece for the Ballets Russes]
```

sections.heading: a. Resources about an individual choreographic work
sections.text:
Assign the name-title or title heading as established in the name authority file to resources about an individual choreographic work. Assign additional headings if necessary to bring out the contents of the resource. Examples:

```
Title: Balanchine's Mozartiana : the making of a masterpiece.
600 10 $a Balanchine, George. $t Mozartiana.

Title: Giselle immortal.
[Photographs of Giselle as choreographed by Marius Petipa and performed by Nadia
Pavlova and Yuri Soloviev]
600 10 $a Petipa, Marius, $d 1818-1910. $t Giselle $v Illustrations.
```

sections.heading: b. Resources about multiple choreographic works
sections.text:
Assign the subject heading as established in sec. 1 above when the resource is about multiple choreographic works, or if it is not possible to determine which individual work is being discussed. Assign additional headings if necessary to bring out the contents of the resource. Examples:

```
Title: Le sacre du printemps : seven productions from Nijinsky to Martha
Graham.
650 #0 $a Rite of spring (Choreographic work)

Title: The staging of Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet as a ballet.
650 #0 $a Romeo and Juliet (Choreographic work)
600 10 $a Shakespeare, William, $d 1564-1616. $t Romeo and Juliet.
600 10 $a Shakespeare, William, $d 1564-1616 $x Stage history.
```
